skills.name: Talking about rights; reading about young parliamentarians

note.text:
Text: The Children's Parliament
Every year, children chosen from schools all over Cameroon meet as members of the Children's Parliament. Like real members of parliament, they debate and vote. This year, Junior Parliamentarian Ayuk Mary spoke about the right to education: "Some girls stop school because they must work at home or marry too young. Every child has the right to go to school, to be healthy, to be protected from violence and to be heard." Another young parliamentarian reminded the house that rights come with duties: "We must respect our parents and teachers, study hard and protect the environment." At the end, the children sent their proposals to the Minister.

A right is something every person should have or be allowed to do (to go to school, to be protected). A duty is something we must do (to respect others, to obey the law).

worked_example.problem: Name two rights and two duties from the text.
steps: Rights: “to go to school, to be healthy, to be protected from violence and to be heard”.
Duties: “respect our parents and teachers, study hard and protect the environment”.
worked_example.answer: rights: education, protection; duties: respect, studying hard

cards.idea: A right is what a child should have; a duty is what a child must do.
example: Right: to go to school. Duty: to study hard.

cards.idea: Find the answer in the text and quote it.
example: Who spoke about education? Ayuk Mary.
The right to education comes with the duty to study.

questions.prompt: Text “The Children's Parliament”. Which statement is wrong?

right.text: The members come from schools all over Cameroon.
The proposals were sent to the Minister.

wrong.text: The Children's Parliament is made of adults.
wrong.explain: Its members are children chosen from schools.

wrong.text: Ayuk Mary said girls should marry young.
wrong.explain: She said marrying too young stops girls' schooling.
